claims.statement: The revised Waste Shipment Regulation and DIWASS went live on 21 May 2026, replacing paper procedures with electronic exchange for covered movements, with a paper transition through 2026.
The Commission designed DIWASS as a central hub able to exchange documents with member-state systems and commercial business software.

contrary_evidence: DIWASS itself offers direct access to operators without software.
Existing waste and TMS vendors are natural integration incumbents, and paper remains temporarily available in 2026.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a corridor-specific library of classification and state-transition exceptions across authorities and systems
fingerprint.customer: cross-border waste brokers, carriers, recovery facilities, and high-frequency industrial waste shippers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: weighbridge software, transport-management vendors, waste brokers, and facility networks
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: DIWASS adapter, document assembly, state machine, acknowledgement reconciliation, and exception queue
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the broker or shipper pays for integration, access, and each routed movement
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a notified or green-listed waste movement needs digital parties, documents, consent status, and completion evidence

founder_fit: Pure integration and state-machine work fits the founder's automation skills, is measurable per movement, and can scale through a few software channels.
risks: Misclassification or missed consent state can interrupt lawful shipment.
The router must never bypass authority approval.

structure.control_point: the acknowledged digital movement record that releases and traces a cross-border waste shipment
structure.critical_dependency: DIWASS interoperability plus correct waste classification, party identity, consent, and facility data

thesis: An API-first router can map weighbridge, carrier, consent, facility, and movement data into DIWASS, watch state changes, and reconcile acknowledgements back into logistics software. Waste brokers and weighbridge vendors reach many shippers; every movement is a paid, recurring transaction.
title: DIWASS Document Router for Cross-Border Waste Operators
uncertainties: Whether incumbents will partner or build directly.
